sentences.text: Shri Satendra Singh Sikarwar - Pp for the State.

Order 
The present petition has been preferred by the petitioners under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.106/2022 registered at Police Station- Sabalgarh, District - Morena for the offence under Sections 363, 376, 120-B, 506/34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of the POCSO and consequential proceedings arising thereto on the basis of compromise.

2 . It appears that parties agreed to settle the matter and therefore, applications vide I.A.
No.3556/2026 and No.3558/2026 have been preferred at the instance of parties and they want to settle the matter.
The applications are duly signed by respective parties and same are supported by their affidavits.
3 . The Principal Registrar of this Court has duly verified the parties, contents of application, intent and signatures of parties.

Report is attached, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7480 2 MCRC-45331-2023 same is perused and it appears that compromise has been reached between the parties voluntarily without any threat, inducement and coercion.

4 . Learned counsel for petitioner submitted that the petitioner No.1/Neelesh @ Narendra and respondent No.2 have solemnized marriage and they are living as husband and wife together and have settled their dispute peacefully.

Therefore, petitioners prayed for quashing of the F.I.R.
registered against them.

5 . Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the documents appended thereto.

sentences.text: 6. A Lean Compromise is better than a Fat Law Suit , instant efforts of the parties indicate the same.
It is expected that their bonafide gestures would continue.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in catena of judgments Jagdish Channa & others Vs. State of Haryana & another, AIR 2008 SC 1968, Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, AIR 2008 SC 1969, Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another, (2011) 10 SCC 705, Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675, Gian Singh Vs.
State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Parbatbhai Ahir alias Parbatbhai Bhimsinhbhai Karmur and others Vs. State of Gujarat and another, (2017) 9 SCC 641, laid down that even in non- compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the court can be saved and utilized in other material cases.
8. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into account NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:7480 3 MCRC-45331-2023 the law laid down by the Apex Court, in the opinion of this Court, continuance of trial in such matter will be a futile exercise which will serve no purpose.
Under such a situation, Section 482 Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the courts below.
